title: S.T.F.U - Skyrim Talk Filter Utility
tagline: Skyrim Talk Filter Utility silences tedious frequent utterances
description:
Skyrim Talk Filter Utility gives you full control over what dialogue you hear in game. Stop repetitive NPC chatter from polluting SkyrimNet's context or interrupting conversations.

## Features
- **Intuitive UI** for viewing all dialogue that plays in game. Block whatever you want instantly.
- **Soft Blocking**: block audio/subtitles from certain dialogue to essentially block it without preventing important scripts from executing. Soft blocked dialogue does not get logged by SkyrimNet *(recommended)*
- **Hard Blocking**: block dialogue from playing at all. Useful for scenes with packages you want to prevent. Can potentially block scripts, use carefully.
- **Subtype Filtering**: block all dialogue belonging to certain subtypes for broad dialogue blocking.
- **Whitelist**: prevent certain dialogue from being blocked under any circumstances to create rule exceptions.\n- **Actor & Faction Filtering**: When blacklisting or whitelisting you can create rules for specific actors or factions.
- **Persistent & Immediate**: Your blacklist and whitelist is stored in an external database that persists between saves. Changes take place immediately, no need to restart.

- **Lite Mode**: If you can't use the PrismaUI menu (or don't want to) you can block dialogue by viewing the STFU_DialogueLog.txt file and adding the topics to the YAMLs. Click \"Import from YAML\" in the MCM to import the entries into the database. See the github page for more details.

## Requirements
- SkyUI (for MCM)
- PrismaUI (for UI)
- SKSE
- Address Library
- powerofthree's Tweaks
author: zevick
changelog:
## Fixes
- Potential fix for a crash during Dragon Rising's scene in Dragonsreach.
- Hard-blocked lines could sometimes slip through on their second part.
- Changing a blocked scene's category no longer leaves it controlled by both toggles until you restart.
- Blocking a topic no longer overrides the toggle of a scene that has its own entry (e.g. a follower commentary or bard scene).
- "Import Scenes" now adds the actual bard song scenes instead of three invalid entries.
- The History tab's "Whitelisted" filter now works.
- NPC names containing quotes no longer break the actor picker.
- Entries that don't match any topic, scene, actor, faction or plugin are no longer saved silently; you get an error message instead. Failed actor filters and unreadable YAML files show an error too, and YAML import now tells you how many entries it imported.
- Fixed a possible crash when reading older history entries.
- Fixed a slow memory leak during long play sessions.
- Much less log spam in STFU.log.
- Bard song scenes added automatically on first launch no longer overwrite changes you made to existing bard entries.
